conventions: Annex A of STORAGE.md, which is normative: an implementation MUST derive these rows for each kind it writes

cases.label: mail, every field present
cases.note: the Date carries a +02:00 offset, so the key and the date column are the UTC instant with the Z designator, never the local reading. attachment is 0 because the writer walked the one text part, and 0 without the body too (meta_attachment), the top-level Content-Type being text/plain (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, Message-ID already claimed in the collection
cases.note: the same body the case above holds, met a second time in one mailbox under another IMAP UID: the hint is taken, so the key is minted (STORAGE §9). Same fixture on purpose, minting depending on the hint and the handle and never on the body; the two items share one object, refcounted twice, and carry identical rows

cases.label: mail, no Message-ID
cases.note: content stating no usable hint takes the kind's fallback in its place: alt:, the decoded subject, the date column and the sender column joined by |, each empty when absent (STORAGE §9, Annex A.1). checks/vectors.py re-derives it; a second such message in one collection mints over it like a hint (vector 31)

cases.label: mail, encoded headers
cases.note: the case that split three writers: an RFC 2047 subject and display name are decoded, a quoted phrase with a comma is one name, and the addr-spec is lowercased whole (Annex A.6) while the name keeps its case. No In-Reply-To gives '[]', never NULL

cases.label: mail, unparseable Date
cases.note: date is NULL rather than guessed, and the empty key lands the message last in a descending listing

cases.label: mail, no Subject header
cases.note: subject is NOT NULL and may be empty, so it is empty rather than NULL; the obsolete GMT zone reads as +0000

cases.label: mail, two In-Reply-To ids
cases.note: In-Reply-To is 1*msg-id (RFC 5322), hence an array; each id loses its angle brackets, like message_id

cases.label: mail, a recent Date
cases.note: the in-scope message of the scoped sync cases (SYNC.md §11); a text/plain message marks 0 with the body and without

cases.label: mail, a Date in the future
cases.note: a clock set ahead: the Date is taken as stated, and a scope with an open ceiling holds it (SYNC.md §5). No Content-Type is text/plain (RFC 2045 §5.2), so no mark

cases.label: mail, multipart/mixed with no attachment
cases.note: a list footer as a second, inline part: without the body the top-level multipart/mixed reads as an attachment (meta_attachment 1), and the walk of the parts finds no Content-Disposition: attachment and replaces it with 0 (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, an attachment
cases.note: a part carrying Content-Disposition: attachment under a multipart/mixed: both derivations give 1 (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, attachments
cases.note: the stand-ins' parts (STORAGE section 14.3, Annex A.7): the parts carrying Content-Disposition: attachment, in document order, by IMAP section (RFC 3501 section 6.4.5), the multipart/alternative being 1 and its children 1.1 and 1.2, the inline image 2 standing for nothing. 3 is named by RFC 2231 continuations, one encoded, and measures 15 decoded octets of base64 across two lines; 4 is named by an RFC 2047 word in its filename, the Content-Disposition filename winning over the Content-Type name, and its quoted-printable soft line break joins the two lines into 13 octets; 5 states no Content-Type, so no media type, and no name, its two identity lines counting the line break between them and not the one before the delimiter (RFC 2046 section 5.1.1)

cases.label: mail, the walk's depth
cases.note: the walk of a message's parts is bounded (STORAGE Annex A.1): multiparts nested 63 deep under the message, the deepest holding an attachment at depth 64, read and stood for, and a multipart at depth 64 holding one at depth 65, never read, so it makes no stand-in

cases.label: mail, the walk's length
cases.note: the walk reads no entity after its 10,000th, the message's own counted (STORAGE Annex A.1): 9,998 bare parts, then an attachment as the 10,000th entity, read and stood for at section 9999, and one as the 10,001st, never read

cases.label: mail, the stand-ins' bound
cases.note: at most 1,000 stand-ins per message (STORAGE section 14.3): 1,001 parts carry the disposition, the walk reads them all and the mark is 1, and the first 1,000 alone are stood for, the 1,001st, section 1001, being left to a reader that finds 1,000

cases.label: mail, an invitation
cases.note: an iMIP request (RFC 6047): the UID of the VEVENT in the text/calendar part, its folded line unfolded, is the invitation; a multipart/alternative with no Content-Disposition: attachment gives 0 both ways (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, a Message-ID without angle brackets
cases.note: a Message-ID with no < is read bracketless: trimmed, holding no whitespace and exactly one @, it is the id, kept as written (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, a bracketless Message-ID that names nothing
cases.note: read bracketless, 4711 at relay holds whitespace and no @, so the field is unparseable: message_id is NULL and the alt: key stands in, never the field's text (Annex A.1, STORAGE §9)

cases.label: mail, comments around the ids
cases.note: comments are skipped, the one before the id holding a < of its own, so the id is comment-1@example.org, never relay@example.net nor the field's raw text; In-Reply-To skips its comment the same way. In From the comment reads as a space and the trimmed display name is Night Ops, the addr-spec lowercased whole (Annex A.1, A.6)

cases.label: mail, an obsolete two-digit year
cases.note: a two-digit year of 50 or more is in the 1900s (RFC 5322 §4.3), so 96 is 1996; the Date states no day of the week, which is optional (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, an obsolete zone name, folded and commented
cases.note: EDT is -0400, so 06:00 is 10:00Z; the Date is folded before its zone and ends in a comment, both ignored, and its two-digit year below 50 is 2026. With no Message-ID the alt: key carries the instant, so a writer reading the zone otherwise keys the message apart (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, a military zone
cases.note: RFC 5322 §4.3 reads a military zone as -0000 whatever RFC 822 made its letter mean, so Q at 10:00 is 10:00Z, never 06:00Z nor 14:00Z; a three-digit year adds 1900, so 126 is 2026 (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, a Date without seconds
cases.note: the seconds are optional and read as 00, so 12:00 at +0200 is 10:00:00Z (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, a day the month lacks
cases.note: 30 February is out of range, so the Date is unparseable and date NULL, never carried into 2 March; the empty key lands the message last (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, a folded and padded Subject
cases.note: the Subject is unfolded, each line break before whitespace removed and the whitespace kept; the two encoded words with whitespace alone between them are joined, a Q underscore being a space; the text after them, a tab included, stays as written, and the ends are trimmed of spaces and tabs. The alt: key carries the subject so read (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, malformed encoded words
cases.note: a B word with a character outside the base64 alphabet, a Q word with an = and no hexadecimal pair after it, and a word whose charset no WHATWG label names each stay as their literal text, the whitespace after them kept; only the last word decodes, read as ok (Annex A.1)

cases.label: mail, raw 8-bit bytes that are no UTF-8
cases.note: the Subject carries raw bytes, no encoded word, read as UTF-8 with each maximal subpart of an ill-formed sequence one U+FFFD (Annex A.0): E9 before a space one, the truncated F0 9F 98 one, C3 before ( one, the overlong C0 AF two and the surrogate ED A0 80 three. The alt: key carries them

cases.label: card, every field present
cases.note: every EMAIL is an address row in document order; a card's addresses carry no name of their own

cases.label: card, full lowercase mapping
cases.note: Annex A.2 and A.6 lowercase by the default full mapping, locale-independent: a dotted capital I becomes i and a combining dot above (U+0069 U+0307), never a bare i, and never the dotless i a Turkish locale gives

cases.label: card, UID already claimed in the collection
cases.note: an address book holding one UID under two resources, which RFC 6352 §5.1 forbids and a server hands over anyway: the second one mints its key. The handle is the resource name, the last segment of the href exactly as the server returned it, percent-escapes included and nothing re-encoded or decoded

cases.label: card, escaped values and a quoted parameter
cases.note: the case that split two writers: FN and ORG are unescaped (RFC 6350 §3.4), the EMAIL's LABEL parameter is quoted around a colon so the property splits on the colon after it (§3.3), the addr-spec is lowercased whole, and the folded NOTE is one line. The key is the unescaped name lowercased

cases.label: card, no FN
cases.note: fn is NOT NULL and may be empty; the empty key sorts a nameless contact first rather than burying it

cases.label: card, a UID beginning with a reserved prefix
cases.note: the UID states an identity that begins like a hash: key; read verbatim it would draw its own seq, never link and take no reference (STORAGE §9), so the link id escapes it with esc:, and the uid column keeps it verbatim

cases.label: card, FN needing case and space normalisation
cases.note: fn keeps FN verbatim, surrounding spaces included, since it is what a reader displays; only the key is lowercased and trimmed. ASCII on purpose (README)

cases.label: event, UTC DTSTART
cases.note: a UTC date-time is already an instant, so the key is the value read straight through

cases.label: event, UID already claimed in the collection
cases.note: the observed shape (STORAGE §A.3): one calendar holding one UID under two resources one client wrote, named event-utc%40example.org.ics and event-utc%2540example.org.ics. Those are two different names and not one name spelled twice, the second literally containing the characters % 2 5 4 0. The first binds the free hint and keeps the bare key, the second mints; the handle is the name as the server returned it, decoded by nobody

cases.label: event, zoned DTSTART on a fall-back fold
cases.note: local 01:30 happens twice in America/New_York; the rule takes the offset in effect BEFORE the transition, EDT at -04:00, the earlier instant. EST would give 06:30:00Z

cases.label: event, zoned DTSTART in a spring-forward gap
cases.note: local 02:30 never happens in America/New_York; RFC 5545 §3.3.5 reads it at the offset in effect BEFORE the transition, EST at -05:00, which is 03:30 EDT on the clock that day, as java.time and Temporal read it. The offset after the gap would give 06:30:00Z

cases.label: event, date-only DTSTART
cases.note: read as T00:00:00Z by convention: an all-day item sorts differently either side of UTC and the writer cannot know which

cases.label: event, floating DTSTART
cases.note: no Z and no TZID, so the wall time is read as UTC

cases.label: event, TZID that will not resolve
cases.note: the TZID names no VTIMEZONE and no known zone, so the time is read as floating rather than dropped: an offset of error, where an empty key would move the item to the far end. dtstart_tzid keeps the parameter verbatim

cases.label: event, a TZID with no VTIMEZONE
cases.note: the resource carries no VTIMEZONE, which RFC 7809 lets it omit for a standard zone, so the IANA time zone database resolves its TZID: Paris is at +02:00 in August, so 09:00 is 07:00:00Z, where reading it as floating would give 09:00:00Z (Annex A.3)

cases.label: event, a VTIMEZONE whose rule steps by the second
cases.note: the zone's DAYLIGHT rule, at +01:00, steps every second from 1970, and its STANDARD observance, at +00:00, has one onset in 1980: followed for 1,000,000 periods the rule's last onset is 1970-01-12T13:46:39, so 1980's +00:00 stands in June 2026 and 12:00 is 12:00:00Z, where following the rule without the bound would give 11:00:00Z after 1.7 billion steps (Annex A.3)

summary.summary: A zone stepping by the second

cases.label: event, recurring with an UNTIL
cases.note: the key is the first occurrence, fixed for the life of the series; until carries the RRULE's UNTIL verbatim, so a reader bounds the series without expanding it

cases.label: todo, DUE and no DTSTART
cases.note: a VTODO is scheduled by DUE and need not carry a DTSTART; the row is task_summary's, and the columns it does not state are NULL; with no CREATED the capture is DTSTAMP

cases.label: todo, both DUE and DTSTART
cases.note: pins the precedence: for a VTODO the key is DUE then DTSTART, so DTSTART is carried but does not decide it

cases.label: todo, organised
cases.note: the columns a task list reads without the body: PRIORITY as an integer; every CATEGORIES value in document order, split on unescaped commas and unescaped, across two properties; CREATED as the capture instant; the parent the first RELATED-TO of type PARENT names, a RELATED-TO with no RELTYPE being one (RFC 5545 section 3.2.15) and a SIBLING not; the message the first mid: URI names (RFC 2392), percent-decoded, an https ATTACH before it skipped. The X- property is kept in the body and in no column; with neither DUE nor DTSTART the sort key is empty

summary.summary: Ask the bank about the card limit

cases.label: todo, captured and waiting on an address
cases.note: revision 2 (Annex A.4): CREATED is the capture even beside a later DTSTAMP, an edit restating DTSTAMP; the CONTACT files a contact address from its mailto: ALTREP, canonical, its text the name

cases.label: todo, waiting on a text
cases.note: revision 2 (Annex A.4): with no CREATED the capture is DTSTAMP; a CONTACT with no ALTREP files its text as the address, lowercased as A.6 keeps a value that is no addr-spec, with the text decoded as the name, and one whose text is an addr-spec files it with no name

cases.label: event, no UID
cases.note: content with no usable UID gets the writer-derived hash: key of Annex A.2, the FNV-1a 64 digest of the bytes, rather than a refusal; checks/vectors.py re-derives it

cases.label: card, a group with an organisation
cases.note: KIND is lowercased, ORG keeps its first component with its escaped semicolon unescaped, the EMAIL is lowercased whole and carries no name; MEMBER is no column

cases.label: event, its people, a recurrence by RDATE and a DURATION
cases.note: ORGANIZER and each ATTENDEE file a row under their role in document order, mailto: stripped and lowercased whole, CN the name; an RDATE alone makes the event recurring, with no until; a DURATION is not resolved, so dtend is null; SUMMARY and LOCATION are unescaped, LOCATION's \n a line break; the TZID names no VTIMEZONE and resolves through the IANA database, +02:00 in October

cases.label: journal, a date-only DTSTART
cases.note: a VJOURNAL fills journal_summary (Annex A.5): its UID, its SUMMARY unescaped and its DTSTART with its parameters; a date reads as midnight UTC for the key
